---
title: "Reproducing the folivory data: from the raw file to the cleaned table"
---

This report shows how `data/clean/folivory_clean.csv` is obtained from the published raw data, and checks each step. To reproduce it, run from the project root:

``` r
renv::restore()      # install the package versions in renv.lock
targets::tar_make()  # clean the data, make the figure, render report.html
```

```{r}
#| label: load-packages
library(ggplot2) # needed to print the stored figure
```

# Data

Muola & Stenberg (2018), Dryad [10.5061/dryad.69r593t](https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.69r593t) (CC0 1.0); paper [10.1002/ece3.4687](https://doi.org/10.1002/ece3.4687).
The raw Excel file in `data/raw/` is never edited.
The two sheets (`data` and the authors' codebook `code`) were exported once to `data/csv/` with no cleaning.

```{r}
#| label: check-data
raw_xlsx <- list.files("data/raw", pattern = "xlsx$", full.names = TRUE)
md5_ok <- unname(tools::md5sum(raw_xlsx)) == "ddf5756b78fc20ea4f7db678166295f1"
csv_ok <- all(vapply(readxl::excel_sheets(raw_xlsx), function(s) {
  x <- as.data.frame(readxl::read_excel(raw_xlsx, sheet = s, .name_repair = "minimal"))
  y <- read.csv(file.path("data/csv", paste0("folivory_", s, ".csv")), check.names = FALSE, na.strings = "")
  isTRUE(all.equal(x, y, check.attributes = FALSE))
}, logical(1)))
```

Checks: the raw file's md5 matches the dataset record (`{r} md5_ok`), and the CSV copies equal the Excel sheets (`{r} csv_ok`).

# Cleaning

`clean_folivory()` (source below) does the cleaning; this cell also defines it for the rest of the document.

```{r}
#| label: clean-function
#| file: R/clean_folivory.R
```

The authors code missing values as `"."`, so read naively six numeric columns become text:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-type-change
#| tbl-cap: "Columns that change type when the CSV is read with `na.strings = c('', '.')`."
naive <- read.csv(targets::tar_read(folivory_csv))
folivory_raw <- targets::tar_read(folivory_raw)
folivory_clean <- targets::tar_read(folivory_clean)

types <- data.frame(
  column = names(naive),
  naive = vapply(naive, function(x) class(x)[1], character(1)),
  with_na_strings = vapply(folivory_raw, function(x) class(x)[1], character(1)),
  dots = vapply(naive, function(x) sum(x == ".", na.rm = TRUE), integer(1))
)
knitr::kable(subset(types, naive != with_na_strings), row.names = FALSE)
```

Cleaning drops no rows (`{r} nrow(folivory_raw)` before, `{r} nrow(folivory_clean)` after), renames columns to snake_case (for example `{r} names(naive)[6]` becomes `{r} names(folivory_clean)[6]`) and turns experimental damage into an ordered factor with levels `{r} paste(levels(folivory_clean$experimental_damage_2013), collapse = " < ")`.
Without `na.strings`, the function stops instead of returning text columns:

```{r}
#| label: guard-example
tryCatch(clean_folivory(naive), error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
```

# Figure

Fruits per plant in the year after the damage treatment (@fig-fruits).
It is descriptive only: no model or test was fitted.
Group medians run from `{r} min(tapply(folivory_clean$number_of_fruits_2014, folivory_clean$experimental_damage_2013, median))` to `{r} max(tapply(folivory_clean$number_of_fruits_2014, folivory_clean$experimental_damage_2013, median))` fruits, and the groups overlap heavily.

```{r}
#| label: fig-fruits
#| fig-cap: "Fruits per plant in 2014 by experimental leaf damage in 2013 (Muola & Stenberg 2018 data). Points are individual plants, jittered sideways; bars are group medians."
targets::tar_read(fruit_figure)
```
